body.estimand_functional: \(\mathcal P(\Sigma)=\{+1:\text{a same-sign sector passes the finite certificate}\}\cup\{-1:\text{an opposite-sign sector passes the finite certificate}\}\)

sampling_model.design: Independent cross-sectional equilibrium sampling from \(dX_t=-AX_tdt+D^{1/2}dW_t\), with known zero mean; \(\operatorname{tr}(D)=1\) selects a representative under common rescaling of \(A\) and \(D\).
sampling_model.treatment: There is no designated treatment; the generator coefficients are \(-A_{12}\) and \(-A_{21}\), whose product has the same sign as \(A_{12}A_{21}\).
sampling_model.overlap: Not applicable; strict diffusion positivity and covariance eigenvalue bounds replace treatment overlap.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The regular nuisance is \(\Sigma\), estimated by \(S_n\); drift and diffusion are not selected pointwise but are existentially profiled through the sector certificate, with \(\eta\) and \(M\) interpreted in the normalized time unit.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 4.2 characterizes pointwise ambiguity of one target edge by membership in its zero-edge signature set.
Global drift identifiability with diagonal volatility holds exactly for simple graphs, and the directed two-cycle has a nontrivial fiber.
The Lyapunov trek rule yields a power-series covariance expansion and acyclic variance inequalities.
Model equivalence and structural identifiability are characterized for acyclic graphical continuous Lyapunov models.
An \(\ell_1\)-regularized Lyapunov estimator has model-selection guarantees under an irrepresentability condition.
Criterion inversion yields confidence regions, consistency, and rates for identified sets.
Directional differentiability determines when the standard bootstrap fails and supports locally valid alternatives.
Weakly regular parameters admit local impossibility results through underlying regular parameters.
Higher-order cumulant equations generically identify the drift under non-Gaussianity and support asymptotically normal estimation.

body.tldr: Stationary Gaussian snapshots identify a covariance but not the drift around a directed feedback cycle when diagonal diffusion is unknown. The project selects one representative of the common time-scale class by imposing \(\operatorname{tr}(D)=1\), interprets \(\eta\) and \(M\) in those normalized units, and characterizes exactly which values of \(\operatorname{sign}(A_{12}A_{21})\) occur on the resulting bounded bivariate Lyapunov fiber. Its focal object is a four-sector certificate that distinguishes feasible, closure-only, and infeasible branches, including equal-variance thresholds and an asymmetric zero-diffusion contact. Covariance-region inversion then gives honest finite-sample set coverage, uniform singleton recovery beyond \(n^{-1/2}\) clearance, and a matching local Gaussian obstruction on compact regular contact subcharts.

project_justification.gap: Van Seeventer and Salehkaleybar characterize signs one drift edge at a time and explicitly leave subgraph and graph-level signs open. Dettling, Homs, Améndola, Drton, and Hansen identify the directed two-cycle as the obstruction to full drift recovery under fixed diagonal volatility, but do not characterize a coarser sign quotient along its affine Lyapunov fiber. Neither result resolves strict-diffusion attainment or sampling uncertainty at the resulting contact sets.
project_justification.niche: The exactly bivariate cycle is the smallest model in which full drift identification fails while a joint causal feature can remain point identified. Common rescaling of \(A\) and \(D\) changes only time units and leaves the stationary covariance and cycle polarity unchanged; trace one fixes that gauge, while \(\eta\) and \(M\) are bounds in the selected units rather than scale-free restrictions.
project_justification.fill: The project first records the common time-scale equivalence and its unique trace-one representative, then derives an exact finite semialgebraic certificate for the compatible loop-polarity set, proves its open-versus-closed branches, gives closed-form equal-variance and asymmetric-contact reductions, and propagates the population set through a Gaussian covariance confidence region with local sharpness at regular contacts.

body.related_work: Van Seeventer and Salehkaleybar (2026, Theorem 4.2, Remark 5.1, and the Conclusion) introduce one-edge signature sets, reduce their feasibility to linear restrictions, and explicitly identify graph-level signs as an open direction; their positive diagonal diffusion setting informs the target map but does not supply or require the trace-one convention used here. Trace one is solely the representative selected by common rescaling of \(A\) and \(D\), and \(\eta\) and \(M\) are imposed after that choice of time units. Dettling, Homs, Améndola, Drton, and Hansen (2023, Example 3.2 and Theorem 4.3) show that the directed two-cycle generates the sharp failure of global drift identification with diagonal volatility; their half-vectorized Lyapunov map informs the affine-fiber reduction. Hansen (2025) gives a trek expansion and acyclic variance inequalities, while the cyclic inverse fiber and its strict boundary topology are outside that result. Dettling, Drton, and Kolar (2024) analyze Lyapunov-lasso model selection from equilibrium snapshots rather than inference on a known graph's compatible sign quotient. Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer (2007) inform confidence-region inversion for set-valued parameters. Fang and Santos (2019) inform nonsmooth boundary analysis, and Kaji (2021) informs the local weak-identification interpretation. Recke and Hansen (2026) recover the full drift using non-Gaussian higher cumulants; Gaussian snapshots remove precisely that extra information and leave the polarity fiber studied here.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The complete equality-active-set proof is the load-bearing unresolved step. It must cover dependent constraint rows, sectors that are lines or points, same-sign equality with \(s=u\), interior-diffusion failure at \(d\in\{0,1\}\), and norm equality without invoking Slater continuity. The early kill tests are the asymmetric \(g=0\) contact with false \(J\), an attained positive equal-variance threshold, and the unattained negative infimum at \(r=1/2\), \(\eta=3/5\), and \(M^2=67/45\). Failure of any branch stops the theorem spine.
body.honest_scope: The project is exactly bivariate and observational. It excludes larger-graph projection, marginalization, empirical performance, and global equivalence between certificate margin and covariance distance. The trace-one restriction fixes common time units only; the substantive magnitude bounds \(\eta\) and \(M\) must be converted whenever a different time unit is used. The population certificate and its inference consequences remain to be proved. The local distance and lower-bound claims are confined to compact regular subcharts of the explicit asymmetric contact. As a reduction outside the two-edge beta-min class, delete one directed edge and its margin condition. The resulting simple cause--effect graph has \(\operatorname{sign}(A_{12})=-\operatorname{sign}(t)\) under the present mean-reversion convention, which is the one-edge covariance-sign formula of van Seeventer and Salehkaleybar after converting their generator sign convention.
